The section also outlines total interest-earning assets and liabilities, highlighting changes in net interest income and interest rate spreads between the two periods. Readers can learn about the bank's financial performance, interest rate trends, and the impact of market conditions on earnings.

children.title: Glossary of Terms and Acronyms and Line of Business Metrics
children.summary: This section provides a comprehensive glossary of terms and acronyms related to financial metrics across various lines of business, including Consumer & Community Banking, Corporate & Investment Bank, Commercial Banking, and Asset & Wealth Management. It details key revenue components such as debit and credit card sales volume, mortgage servicing revenue, and investment banking fees. Additionally, it outlines the origination channels for mortgage loans and the client types served in different banking segments. Performance measures for asset management, including mutual fund ratings and quartile rankings, are also highlighted, offering insights into the effectiveness of investment strategies.

children.title: Line of Business Metrics
children.summary: This section outlines key metrics for various lines of business within a financial institution, including Consumer & Community Banking (CCB), Corporate & Investment Bank (CIB), Commercial Banking (CB), and Asset & Wealth Management (AWM). It details specific revenue components such as debit and credit card sales volume, mortgage servicing revenue, and investment banking fees. Additionally, it describes the origination channels for mortgage loans and the types of clients served across different banking segments. The section also highlights performance measures for asset management, including mutual fund ratings and quartile rankings, providing insights into the effectiveness of investment strategies.

children.title: Item 3. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk.
children.summary: This section refers readers to the Market Risk Management section of Management’s discussion and analysis and pages 135–142 of JPMorgan Chase’s 2020 Form 10-K for detailed quantitative and qualitative disclosures about market risk. It emphasizes the importance of understanding the firm's exposure to market fluctuations and the methodologies used to assess these risks. Additionally, it highlights the potential impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on market conditions and the firm's financial performance, including disruptions in financial markets and increased credit loss allowances.

children.title: Item 4. Controls and Procedures.
children.summary: This section discusses the evaluation of the effectiveness of JPMorgan Chase's disclosure controls and procedures, conducted by the Firm's management, including the CEO and CFO. They concluded that these controls were effective as of the report's end date. The section also emphasizes the Firm's commitment to high standards of internal control over financial reporting, while acknowledging inherent limitations that may lead to misstatements. Additionally, it notes that there were no significant changes in internal control during the reporting period that could materially affect financial reporting.

children.title: Part II – Other information
children.summary: Part II provides an overview of various important disclosures related to JPMorgan Chase, including ongoing legal proceedings, material risk factors influenced by the COVID-19 pandemic, and the status of equity securities and share repurchase programs. It confirms no defaults on senior securities and states that mine safety disclosures are not applicable. Additionally, it includes a section on other information, indicating no further disclosures beyond what has been previously reported, and lists exhibits related to financial certifications and reports, including compliance with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and XBRL documents for financial data.

children.title: Item 1. Legal Proceedings.
children.summary: This section references the material legal proceedings involving JPMorgan Chase, directing readers to Note 24 of the Form 10-Q for updates on disclosures previously outlined in the 2020 Form 10-K. It emphasizes the importance of understanding ongoing legal challenges that may impact the firm's operations and financial condition. The section serves to keep stakeholders informed about potential legal risks and their implications for the firm.

children.title: Item 1A. Risk Factors.
children.summary: This section discusses the material risk factors affecting JPMorgan Chase, supplementing the previous disclosures in its 2020 Form 10-K. It highlights the significant impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the global economy, including disruptions in financial markets, supply chains, and business operations. The pandemic has led to reduced demand for the firm's products and services, resulting in lower revenues and increased credit loss allowances. Additionally, it addresses the heightened performance risk associated with credit loss models due to the pandemic's economic effects, emphasizing the uncertainty of potential unexpected losses.

children.title: Item 2. Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities and Use of Proceeds.
children.summary: This section reports that JPMorgan Chase did not have any unregistered sales of equity securities during the first quarter of 2021. It details the firm's common share repurchase program, which was authorized for up to $30 billion following the Federal Reserve's announcement allowing large banks to resume share repurchases. The section provides specific data on the number of shares repurchased, average prices, and total purchase amounts for January, February, and March 2021, as well as the remaining authorized repurchase amount. Additionally, it notes that repurchases and dividends were restricted to the average net income of the previous four quarters, with these restrictions extended through at least the second quarter of 2021.

children.title: Item 3. Defaults Upon Senior Securities.
children.summary: This section states that there are no defaults upon senior securities, indicating that the company is in compliance with its obligations related to senior securities. It serves to inform stakeholders that there are no current issues or defaults that could affect the company's financial standing or obligations. The section is brief and straightforward, confirming the absence of any defaults.

children.title: Item 4. Mine Safety Disclosures.
children.summary: This section, Item 4, Mine Safety Disclosures, states that it is not applicable for the reporting period. As a result, there are no mine safety disclosures provided in this document. Readers will learn that the company did not encounter any mine safety issues that require reporting under this item.

children.title: Item 5. Other Information.
children.summary: Item 5 contains no additional information beyond what has been previously disclosed. It serves as a placeholder indicating that there are no further disclosures required or provided in this section. The section transitions to Item 6, which lists various exhibits related to financial information and certifications. Notably, it includes a letter regarding unaudited interim financial information and several certifications required under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. Additionally, it references XBRL documents that contain financial data for the firm, formatted for interactive data reporting.

children.title: Item 6. Exhibits.
children.summary: This section lists the exhibits included in the document, detailing various financial certifications and reports. Key items include a letter regarding unaudited interim financial information, certifications under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, and multiple XBRL taxonomy extension documents related to financial reporting. The section also notes that certain documents are incorporated by reference from previous filings, providing context for the financial data presented. Readers can learn about the specific financial disclosures and compliance certifications relevant to JPMorgan Chase & Co.

children.title: Signature
children.summary: This section contains the official signature of JPMorgan Chase & Co. as required by the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. It includes the name and title of the signatory, Elena Korablina, who is the Managing Director and Firmwide Controller, serving as the Principal Accounting Officer. The date of the signature is also provided, indicating when the report was signed, which is May 4, 2021. This section serves to authenticate the report and confirm that it has been duly authorized by the registrant.

children.title: Exhibit 15
children.summary: Exhibit 15 contains a communication from PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP to the Securities and Exchange Commission regarding JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s registration statements on Forms S-3 and S-8. The document, dated May 4, 2021, states that the firm's report on interim financial information is incorporated by reference in the registration statements but should not be considered part of them according to Rule 436(c) of the Securities Act of 1933. This section clarifies the legal standing of the report in relation to the registration statements and outlines the specific registration numbers involved.

children.title: Exhibit 31.1
children.summary: Exhibit 31.1 contains a certification by James Dimon, Chairman and CEO of JPMorgan Chase & Co., regarding the accuracy and completeness of the company's Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q. Dimon certifies that the report does not contain any misleading statements and that the financial statements fairly present the company's financial condition and results of operations. The section outlines the responsibilities of the certifying officers in establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting. It also details the evaluation of these controls and any significant deficiencies or fraud related to financial reporting. This certification is dated May 4, 2021.

children.title: Exhibit 31.2
children.summary: Exhibit 31.2 contains a certification by Jennifer Piepszak, the Chief Financial Officer of JPMorgan Chase & Co., regarding the accuracy and completeness of the Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q. It affirms that the report does not contain any misleading statements and that the financial statements fairly present the company's financial condition and results. The certification also outlines the responsibilities for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting, including evaluations of their effectiveness and any changes that may have occurred. Additionally, it addresses the disclosure of any significant deficiencies or fraud related to internal controls.

children.title: Exhibit 32
children.summary: Exhibit 32 contains a certification by JPMorgan Chase & Co. officers, including CEO James Dimon and CFO Jennifer Piepszak, affirming compliance with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. The certification states that the Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the period ending March 31, 2021, meets the requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. It also asserts that the report accurately reflects the company's financial condition and operational results. This document serves as a formal assurance of the integrity of the financial reporting by the company.
